note: New dxmt9-policy case added 2026-08-02 to cover palettized IDirect3DDevice9::UpdateSurface, which had no conformance coverage at all. It fails DETERMINISTICALLY before the fix -- 5/5 runs, always the same 32 of 213 checks (all four texels x two draws x four invocations: P8/A8P8 x fixed-function/ps_2_0), which is why a small run set suffices where the sibling UpdateTexture defect needed 20+. The two pre-fix runs `head-1` and `head-diag` are today's HEAD plus the new case only; `branch-removed-1..3` are the full fix tree with only the routing branch in dxmt9c_device_update_surface removed, i.e. a control for that branch specifically. `head-diag` carried a temporary printf of the readback values, reverted afterwards; it prints alongside the comparison and cannot influence it. Measured values, identical in every failing run: the FIRST draw (base palette) returns initPalettizedTexture's identity ramp -- ff010101/ff020202/ff030303/ff040404 for P8 indices {1,2,3,4}, and 80010101/40020202/20030303/10040404 for A8P8 (RGB identity, source alpha preserved) -- proving the SOURCE texture's derived expansion was transported. The SECOND draw, after SetPaletteEntries(1,..)+SetCurrentTexturePalette(1), returns ff000000 for P8 and 00000000 for A8P8, i.e. palette[0] everywhere: the destination texture's p8Levels index shadow was never written, so re-expansion at palette-switch time read a still-zero shadow and the copy vanished entirely. That second failure is the more destructive of the two and is the reason D9CSurface's lack of palette state matters. Post-fix the case passes 18/18: 12 runs on an interim variant that fell through to Device::updateSurface when the index copy could not be served, and 6 runs on the final code, which returns D3DERR_INVALIDCALL there instead so a palettized pair can never reach the routed path. Only the 6 `final-*` runs correspond to the shipped winemetal.so (93fbc24b1d04d09d). d3d9.dll and winemetal.dll are byte-identical across every run listed here (b9af3a64ab8f15a0 / 0168db1185e5e377): the change is entirely unix-side, which is itself a check that the right artifact moved.
